anya: Heads-up — after the model bump to checkpoint v3.4.1 in staging we see a p99 latency jump ~2x and GPU alloc churn. Rollout paused.
carl: Can you paste the staging profiler / logs? Which path is regressing (generation, embeddings, or kv hotpath)?
anya: Generation. Short repro attached from the perf harness. Quick excerpt from runtime profiler:
```
2026-03-17T19:14:02Z profiler: batch_size=4 kernel_selected=ref_matmul_64
2026-03-17T19:14:02Z kv_cache: miss_rate=0.23 warmup_hits=0.05
2026-03-17T19:14:03Z tokenizer: avg_tokens=1.8 -> 5.6 (post-onboard)
2026-03-17T19:14:03Z alloc: p50=12MB p99=78MB
```
Looks like tokenizer changes increased short-token fragmentation and the kernel selector fell back to the reference kernel for small sequences. Also KV miss rate spiked for warm prefixes.
jordan: CI perf job also flagged this. ci-bot, can you link the failed bench run?
ci-bot: perf-ci: build/bench/staging/1969998765 failed — regression +47% p99 compared to baseline. See https://ci.internal/redwood/bench/1969998765
sam: If kernel selector is choosing ref kernel due to token length distribution, we might be able to patch selector heuristics quickly (prefer fast_matmul when sequence_len <= 8 and batch >= 2). Otherwise revert the onboard.
carl: Is the tokenizer mapping the cause (different tokenization producing more tokens per prompt) or is it emitting lower-quality prefix caching keys? Any diffs from tokenizer config?
anya: Diff from onboard commit (hash abc1234): tokenizer.normalization=true, added merges for rare unicode sequences. That made average tokens/short-utterance go up from ~1.8 to ~5.6 in our sample corpus.
jordan: Bisect-ish: switching model artifact back to v3.4.0 in staging restores p99 to baseline. That isolates the regression to the onboarded checkpoint/tokenizer combo.
devops-bot: We can shadow-route 20% to the previous model in staging via flag: `route.model=checkpoint:v3.4.0@shadow=0.2` — if you want I can stage that to validate rollback impact.
anya: Please do devops-bot. Also opening a revert PR for the onboard commit now unless we prefer a selector patch first. Revert will unblock rollout quicker.
sam: Quick mitigation: set env `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=prefer_fast_for_short` on the affected pool and force kv prefetch for warm prefixes: `kv.prefetch=true` — that should buy time.
carl: Add a tokenizer regression test to the onboarding pipeline: sample 10k short prompts and assert median tokens/utterance doesn't increase by >20%. Also add a unit test for kernel-selection thresholds.
jordan: Agreed. I'll add CI tests and a perf harness job that runs after tokenization model changes. Also adding a check that onboarding artifacts include tokenizer diff in the release notes.
anya: OK creating PRs: revert-onboard-abc1234 and kernel-hint-hotfix. Will coordinate with SRE to hotpatch staging. After revert we'll run the full perf harness and postmortem. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks — ping me when the hotpatch is applied, I'll run the regression harness locally.
anya: Will do. Closing for now, tracking in #incidents if it blows up.
